verdict.root_cause: The customer-visible failures are 15-second stalls that begin and end inside the frontend process. In both failing traces the entire ~15s is self-time on the frontend handler span, which is a leaf with no child spans at all, while the proxy ingress and router egress spans contribute near-zero self-time and only carry the error because that is where the timeout was enforced [tr_6b7a362b5bc2]. Frontend is therefore stalling before it ever dispatches a downstream call, intermittently: fast successes (6-52ms, including a sibling product-catalog branch inside the same failing trace) interleave with all-or-nothing 15s hangs, and there is no latency ramp [tr_6b7a362b5bc2]. That bimodal pattern matches the bursty, two-phase error ratio at the proxy (mean ~4.4%, peak ~15%, min 0, sd > mean) rising from an exactly flat zero baseline [tr_340936d9adc8], and the much smaller frontend-side error ratio [tr_79ca5b11ec3b] is consistent with frontend not recording the timeout itself. No frontend change of any kind is recorded [tr_7180be4300e6], and the shipping-quote/email-400 log signature [tr_8e876ea73e3a] is a separate, lower-severity issue that cannot be the stall path: no shipping, quote or email spans appear in any of the 116 spans examined [tr_6b7a362b5bc2], and email itself served only 200s with millisecond latencies throughout [tr_9328e45ce586]. The best-supported mechanism is frontend request handlers intermittently blocking on an exhausted local resource (event-loop/worker or connection-pool slot) until the 15s client deadline fires.
verdict.reasoning: Localisation is strong: the 15s is frontend self-time with no children, so no instrumented dependency and no proxy hop is waiting [tr_6b7a362b5bc2]. Change-driven explanations are weak: frontend has no recorded changes [tr_7180be4300e6], email none [tr_8c7186360bf2], and shipping's only entries are automation image toggles that net to no change and end 3.3h before onset [tr_3fe7069b5c94]. The email-400 chain named in frontend logs [tr_8e876ea73e3a] is contradicted as the stall path by the trace topology and by email's own all-200 millisecond-latency logs [tr_9328e45ce586]. Intermittency with concurrent healthy requests in the same process points to a contended, exhaustible local resource rather than a uniformly wrong value or a dead process. Confidence is low because no frontend saturation metric (heap, event-loop lag, pool utilisation, fd count) was ever measured - the mechanism is inferred from trace shape alone.
open_questions: No frontend resource metrics were collected: heap, CPU, event-loop lag, thread/connection-pool utilisation and fd counts are entirely unmeasured, so resource_exhaustion is inferred rather than observed.

Frontend's own logs were queried but only the gRPC/email-400 signature was reported; whether frontend logged anything at all during the 18:18:45 and 18:19:15 stalls is unknown, which leaves a silent-process explanation unexcluded.
All change windows began at the alert timestamp and ran forward, so the pre-onset hours - the interval that would contain a triggering change - were never examined for frontend or email.

alternatives.root_cause: Frontend's process intermittently stops scheduling work while its socket keeps accepting, so callers hang to the 15s deadline.
alternatives.why_not: A sibling request completed in 4.3ms inside the same trace as a stalled one [tr_6b7a362b5bc2], so the process was scheduling work throughout; a true freeze would stall every concurrent request.

alternatives.root_cause: Shipping's quote path sends a request the email service rejects with 400, and frontend surfaces the resulting gRPC INTERNAL to users.
alternatives.why_not: Explains the frontend log signature [tr_8e876ea73e3a] but not the severity-driving 15s timeouts: no shipping or email spans appear in any failing trace [tr_6b7a362b5bc2], email logged only 200s [tr_9328e45ce586], and no shipping config change exists to revert [tr_3fe7069b5c94].

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating the frontend container should clear the in-process state holding handlers to the 15s deadline. Observable as: no further trace with a childless frontend GET/POST span at ~15000ms self-time; frontend-proxy error ratio back to its flat-zero baseline with no crossing above 5%. Bursty errors mean a quiet minute proves nothing - needs a stretch of traffic longer than the previous inter-spike gap.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified by any new ~15s childless frontend span, or a fresh proxy error-ratio crossing above 5%, inside the window. If stalls stop then return after minutes, the cause re-accumulates and restart is a mask. The mechanism itself stays unobservable: heap, CPU, event-loop lag, pool and fd counts were never collected, so recovery would not confirm resource_exhaustion.
proposal.risk: If the stall is driven by something outside the frontend process (host-level contention, an uninstrumented blocking dependency, a client-side deadline change), the restart discards frontend cache, causes a cold-start latency bump, and burns the live evidence of the stalled process without fixing anything. Not reversible.
proposal.blast_radius: frontend only, for the recreate duration. frontend-proxy, its sole inbound caller in this graph, sees connection resets; load-generator traffic through it fails for that interval, briefly raising the same proxy error ratio used to confirm the fix.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerting at the edge proxy with the load generator seeing it too means user-facing impact, not a synthetic-only artifact. No open incident covers it and the one-hop candidate upstream is unverified, so it warrants investigation.
